architecture_feedback: Prefer isolated control plane inside customer's VPC using VPC endpoints (no public internet control plane).
Inbound: only PrivateLink interface endpoints from Redwood control plane to customer's management subnet; data path initiates from customer VPC outbound.
Outbound: egress NAT to customer egress with strict allowlist for Redwood component health checks only.
KMS: must support customer-managed KMS key (bring-your-own-key) for envelope encryption; Redwood needs KMS Decrypt/Encrypt limited IAM role.
Audit logs: delivery of request/response hashes and operational logs to customer's secure S3 (or equivalent) with retention controls; show sample log format.
Regions: primary eu-west-1, DR in eu-central-1; no cross-region data replication without explicit consent.
Networking ask: support for Transit Gateway or VPC peering if PrivateLink is impractical for certain accounts.
vpc_topology_notes: Customer suggested topology: two private subnets for inference workers, one management subnet for control-plane endpoints, dedicated bastion subnet locked to Security team's IPs.
Preferred flow: app -> internal ALB -> inference ENIs -> S3/kms within same VPC; control messages via VPC Endpoint to Redwood control plane.
No inbound internet allowed to inference subnets; only outbound to Redwood-managed endpoints via interface endpoints or NAT with egress allowlist.
Measurement targets to include p95 latency (150ms) and cold-start warmup goals for quantized models.
Customer asked for diagram examples showing PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway tradeoffs; SE to supply two diagram options.
